trust_decision.summary: The agent decides whether a pre-existing object on its predictable run-folder path (base run dir, <agent>_io dir, per-workload control_interface dir, input/output FIFOs, workload files dir/file) may be reused; at the pinned commit it reuses anything that exists (exists()/is_fifo() only) and even chmods the default base dir 0777.

landing_point.why: The summary names Control Interface FIFOs under a predictable path; Fifo::new is where an existing FIFO is silently reused ('Reusing existing fifo file').

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report is about Control Interface FIFOs; the workload `files` mount feature is a separate module that never touches FIFOs, and its files live in a subfolder of the (now checked) workload dir, so a solver can argue it is already covered by the parent-directory check and needs no own symlink/owner check on the final file.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Resuming workloads after an agent restart must keep reusing the existing per-workload control_interface dir and input/output FIFOs owned by the agent (the container still has them bind-mounted); an over-broad fix that rejects or deletes/recreates any existing FIFO/dir breaks resume, as does rejecting a user-supplied run_folder that is agent-owned 0700, or rejecting reuse of an existing agent-owned regular workload file.

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The fix's own check is in the 'already exists' else-branch; the 'we just created it' branch looks trusted by construction.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Directory ownership checks (path.exists() and the new is_owner_exclusive) use metadata(), which follows symlinks, so a planted symlink at the predictable base path to a dir that the agent user owns with mode 0700 passes and redirects the run folder (and the recursive delete in Drop) there; only the workload-file check uses symlink_metadata.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The target must already be agent-owned and private, so it looks 'secure'; the advisory only lists symlinks for workload files.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Control Interface pipes are reopened by path name after the Fifo::new check (OutputPipe::ensure_file on broken pipe, InputPipe::ensure_file on EOF), a check-then-use pair the fix does not revalidate.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Reopen is legitimate reconnect behaviour inside a dir that is now checked to be 0700 agent-owned; argued as already protected by the parent check.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package (control_interface), different files from fifo.rs (also agent/src/control_interface/input_pipe.rs:99-106)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Workload-dir deletion on workload delete does remove_dir_all on the predictable pipes_folder_name path with no ownership/symlink check; a planted copy that also (re)creates a per-workload state/log file there would be a realistic sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Runtime facade already owns the workload subfolder lifecycle; a maintainer adding e.g. a workload log or status file would naturally write it there with filesystem::make_dir/write_file rather than Directory.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second async writer (e.g. write_file_with_mode or an append helper) in filesystem_async used by a new feature, missing is_safe_write_target.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: filesystem_async is the shared write primitive; adding a variant there for a new workload artefact is an ordinary change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An additional per-workload FIFO/socket (e.g. a logs or events channel) created next to input/output via a separate helper instead of Fifo::new.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: InputOutput is the natural place to add another pipe; a maintainer could create it with nix mkfifo directly as tests in input_pipe.rs already do.
